page.layout: One page of verse in italic, set as a block of stanzas; below it a signature line of the author's name and title, centred; then a printed ornament (fleuron) and the division word LIBER at the right, below the text. No margin notes.

p.i: Ipse tibi satis vnus eris quoque, purius illud Ingenij lumen rebus praeferre gerendis. Sistatues: ne corporea quae nubila mole Exiftunt, diu corrumpant lucis honorem.

Si tibi diuina fuerit virtute voluptas Posterior, folidis fi fluxa pecunia rebus: Sic introspiciens turpi fecernere honestum Discès, & quae sunt vere bona, queque videntur, Nec sunt, indicio atque notis distinguere certis.
Quid possis aut non possis, cui fecerit aptum Te natura minúsve rei, cui longior vsus: Sic pelles externa regésque domestica victor, Nec fallent aliy, nec tu te denique falles.

page.notes: The first stanza's line endings and the words "Ingenij", "Sistatues:ne", "Exiftunt" and "Discès" follow the scan as set; the italic text is partly faint. The line "Sic pelles externa regésque" and "Nec fallent aliy" are read as printed (possible faint letters). The ornament (fleuron) is a printed decorative element and not transcribed as text.
